title: Diabetes - MedlinePlus
cleanedText:
Diabetes is a condition where your body has trouble controlling blood sugar (glucose). Glucose comes from food and gives you energy. Insulin is a hormone made by the pancreas that helps glucose enter your cells. In diabetes, the body does not make enough insulin or cannot use insulin well, so glucose stays in the blood.

Symptoms include feeling very thirsty, urinating often, feeling very hungry, feeling tired, having blurry vision, and having cuts or sores that heal slowly. Some people have no symptoms at first, so diabetes may not be found until a routine checkup or blood test. Type 1 diabetes often starts in childhood or young adulthood, while type 2 is more common in adults and is linked to family history, weight, and activity level.

You can manage diabetes by following a meal plan, being active most days of the week, checking blood sugar as advised, and taking medicines or insulin if prescribed. Keep regular appointments, bring your blood sugar log and medication list, and ask about foot and eye checks. See a doctor right away if you have very high blood sugar readings, signs of low blood sugar such as shakiness, sweating, or confusion, fever with high blood sugar, or sores that do not heal.
